query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The wear resistance and microscopic deformation of a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating on a conventional metal substrate during sliding in the high-temperature operating regime are governed by the coating's grain size and the substrate's surface roughness.
generation.material_initial_state: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating with an initial grain size of 10 μm and a substrate surface roughness of 0.5 μm
generation.intervention: Reciprocating wear test with varying temperatures (20°C to 500°C) and coating thicknesses (5 μm to 20 μm)
generation.conditions: High-temperature operating regime (200°C to 500°C), sliding speed of 0.1 m/s, and normal load of 10 N
generation.structural_mediator: Grain size and substrate surface roughness
generation.mechanism: The smaller grain size and smoother substrate surface roughness lead to increased wear resistance and reduced microscopic deformation due to the reduced stress concentration and improved coating-substrate adhesion
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% increase in wear resistance and a 30% reduction in microscopic deformation compared to the baseline coating condition
generation.baseline: FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy thin coating with a grain size of 20 μm and a substrate surface roughness of 1.0 μm
generation.boundary: The predicted outcome should hold within the high-temperature operating regime (200°C to 500°C) and for coating thicknesses between 5 μm and 20 μm
generation.uncertainty: The actual wear resistance and microscopic deformation may vary depending on the specific coating deposition method, substrate material, and testing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Reciprocating wear test with varying temperatures and coating thicknesses
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the wear rate increases by more than 10% or the microscopic deformation increases by more than 20% compared to the baseline coating condition, the hypothesis is falsified

limitation.phenomenon: governing mechanisms of wear resistance and deformation
